A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text and Appendices A–G. Equations, figures, tables and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices D–F report original simulations evaluating transformer state estimation and output prediction against classical estimators.

after.justification: v3 retains those original simulation results and adds a parameter-withholding experiment in Appendix E.5.

M1.justification: The transformer architectures, training objectives, frozen in-context prediction procedure and RAW-based filtering construction remain unchanged. The additional input-removal experiment tests the existing approach.

E1.justification: Appendix E.5 adds prediction from past measurements alone, withholding measurement matrices H_t alongside F, Q and R. The missing-parameter scenarios in v2 retain H_t. The underlying system families remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Figure 12 adds an explicitly n=8 Kalman-filter reference to the parameter-withholding comparison. In v2 Figure 5, the n=8 curves contain ICL and SGD, while the Kalman-filter curve is labeled n=2. No new baseline family is introduced.

E3.justification: Appendix E.5 adds a controlled comparison at n=8 under both system-generation strategies, contrasting full parameters, F/Q/R omission and measurements-only context using normalized MSE versus context length. Reported settings for retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Appendix E.5 ablation tests whether prediction depends on supplied measurement matrices, extending the existing parameter-withholding analysis. Earlier distribution-shift, dimensionality, capacity and multi-step analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 adds no seed counts, repeated-run statistics, confidence intervals or significance tests. The uncertainty-reporting practice in the retained figures and tables is unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 12 adds measurements-only prediction results showing higher error, particularly under Strategy 1. All earlier plot images and numerical entries in Tables 1–2 are retained unchanged; v2 Figure 12 becomes v3 Figure 13.

T1.justification: Equation (8) corrects misplaced transposes and multiplication order in the SGD update, making it consistent with the stated vector dimensions. The Kalman, Dual Kalman, EKF and RAW constructions and derivations are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the central claims about transformer filtering, nonlinear prediction, robustness to partially missing parameters and dependence on model capacity and context length.

C2.justification: New passages explicitly distinguish representability arguments from learning or convergence guarantees. v3 also states limitations from missing inputs and explains why regularization makes Ridge's double-descent behavior milder than OLS.

D1.justification: The code-access hyperlink changes from an OSF share in v2 to a GitHub repository in v3. Existing implementation descriptions, optimizer settings and training curricula are retained.

R1.justification: The same 28 cited works and substantive comparisons with earlier filtering, transformer and state-space research remain. Conversion from numbered to author–year citations does not change research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds a scope-and-framing paragraph, explanatory qualifications and Appendix E.5, while retaining the overall section organization. It also refines the RAW description, standardizes notation and corrects references from expression (51) to (20).

P2.justification: The single-column organization and existing figure/table designs remain. v3 applies TMLR styling, changes the title block and running headers, reflows displays, numbers Algorithm 1 lines and adds a two-panel Figure 12 combining retained conditions with the new ablation.

improvement.justification: Appendix E.5 provides useful evidence that withholding measurement matrices causes additional prediction error beyond withholding F, Q and R. Clearer distinctions between representability and learning guarantees, together with the corrected SGD equation, improve precision and interpretation. These are limited gains alongside an unchanged core method and retained experimental results.
